title: 20-Minute Creamy Tomato Basil Soup That Saved My Sanity
description: Need a fast dinner? This easy 20-minute creamy tomato basil soup uses pantry staples for the ultimate cozy comfort food night. 1 pot, zero stress.
story: If my nine-hour workday had a physical form, it would be a tangled pile of laundry and a cold cup of coffee left on my desk. By the time I finally dragged myself into my tiny kitchen, DoorDash wanted twenty-eight dollars just to deliver a mediocre burrito. Absolutely not. I opened the pantry, saw a lonely can of crushed tomatoes, and decided I was making this creamy tomato basil soup from scratch. It literally takes twenty minutes, uses just one pot so cleanup is basically nonexistent, and hits every single craving. The first time I tested this recipe, I rushed the garlic and burned it to a crisp in my skillet—so trust me, keep the heat medium-low and let it bloom slowly. Poured into a mug with a side of toasted sourdough, it completely salvaged a chaotic Tuesday night.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Kerrygold unsalted butter (or olive oil)
1 can (28 ounces) San Marzano crushed tomatoes
1.5 cups chicken broth or vegetable broth
1/2 cup heavy cream (or full-fat canned coconut milk)
1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped
instructions: Step 1: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat. Toss in the minced garlic and sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant and just turning golden—don't let it burn or it will taste bitter!

Step 2: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then turn the heat down to low and let it bubble uncovered for about 10 minutes so the flavors meld.
Step 3: Stir in the heavy cream and fresh basil. Let it warm through for another 2 minutes until the soup turns a gorgeous, creamy peach color.
Step 4: Season with kosher salt and black pepper to taste. Ladle straight into your favorite mug or bowl and serve immediately.
proHack: Stir in your heavy cream off the direct heat source. If the soup is boiling furiously when the dairy hits the pot, it can curdle and look grainy. A gentle warm-up keeps it silky smooth.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally. Avoid boiling or the cream might separate.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the heavy cream if I don't have dairy?
faqs.answer: Totally! You can use full-fat canned coconut milk, cream cheese, or even oat milk mixed with a little extra butter to keep it rich and creamy.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the tomato soup from splattering all over my stove?
faqs.answer: Simmer it on a lower heat setting with the lid slightly ajar, leaving enough room for steam to escape without turning your backsplash red.
